root_causes: Entity name transliteration mismatch: the true caption text uses '流里个浪' instead of the question's '波里个浪', so exact-match SQL and semantic_search on the given name fail at the correct location.

The only DB evidence for Baw-Li-Guhh-Lang's defeat is implicit (a character-catalog entry appearing after a monster collapses) rather than an explicit '已击败' banner like the other three bosses have, making its exact position genuinely harder to pin down even when the right time window is found.

Two unrelated later-chapter event_chains are mislabeled with 'frog/toad boss fight' in their chain names, actively misleading semantic_search and JOIN queries that key on the word 'frog'/'toad' toward wrong, much-later time windows (~9000s and ~53700-54200s).

Rollouts that succeeded or scored partial credit used a blanket SQL time-window sweep of episodes.text (not semantic_search or exact-name LIKE, and not the terser event_steps.description) across the clue span; rollouts that never did this blanket sweep (0, 1) scored 1.
Rollout 0, unable to find real evidence, defaulted to the same order the bosses were listed in the question -- a give-up heuristic rather than surfacing genuine uncertainty.
what_worked: Rollout 2's exhaustive, brute-force SQL sweep of episodes.text over the full 1800-5100s clue span (independent of exact name matching) surfaced the only usable evidence for Baw-Li-Guhh-Lang.
Rollout 2 also explicitly checked and ruled out the 53700-54150s decoy window before finalizing its answer, avoiding the trap that caught rollout 1.
transferable_lessons: When semantic_search and exact-name SQL LIKE both fail to find a named entity, fall back to a blanket time-window sweep of the raw episodes.text (the richest/longest column) over the clue span rather than giving up or guessing -- entity names in captions can be mis-transliterated.

Treat event_chain/step names containing generic category words (e.g. 'frog', 'toad', 'boss fight') as decoys to verify, not trust directly -- cross-check that the time window is plausible for the question's context (e.g. still within the Black Wind Mountain arc, not thousands of seconds later in a different chapter) before accepting a chain name at face value.

When one item in an ordered set has much weaker evidence (implicit catalog mention) than the other items (explicit victory banners), flag that item's position as the most uncertain rather than asserting a confident placement.

Prefer sweeping episodes.text over event_steps.description when hunting for a specific proper name in captions, since event_steps descriptions are terser and can omit name mentions present in the fuller episode captions.
